content.text:
Looking at F3_Z01 (Zone_F3_Z01) vs other zones, the temperature drift is real in the data — relative to peer zones the gap is ~ -0.4 °C around July 2018 and grows to ~ +2 °C by Nov 2018 / Jan 2019. But the available store for this zone contains only:

- `Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor` (a single room-air temperature)
- `Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Cooling_Temperature_Setpoint` (≈ 25.2 °C, unchanged)
- `Zone_F3_Z01.Zone_Air_Heating_Temperature_Setpoint` (≈ 18.5 °C, unchanged)

No redundant sensor, no occupancy/CO₂, no VAV damper position, no fan/airflow, no electrical load — so a single-sensor temperature drift is equally consistent with "the room got locally warmer (load change)" and with "this sole sensor drifted". With only one temperature signal per zone, the two causes cannot be told apart from the data present.

input.needed_streams: Zone_F3_Z01 redundant / second Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor (or a supply-air temperature near the zone) and a local-load signal for the zone (e.g. Zone_Carbon_Dioxide_Sensor, zone electrical load / plug-load, VAV terminal damper position or Zone_Airflow_Sensor) to distinguish a genuine local load change from a single-sensor temperature-fault.
